oneLine: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by a quarter point on September 16—its first hike in over three years—while Congress advanced bills on crypto taxes and Bitcoin reserves, and cryptocurrency markets absorbed the news with modest gains as traders parsed signals on future rate decisions.
caveman: The Federal Reserve decided to make borrowing money more expensive by raising interest rates. This is normally bad for people buying risky things like cryptocurrency, but Bitcoin and Ethereum actually went up a tiny bit because the Fed said it might not raise rates too much more. Stocks fell about half a percent, while gold went up (people buy gold when worried). Congress also voted on new ideas for taxing cryptocurrency and making the US government hold Bitcoin forever. It was a day about policy and big decisions, not emergencies.
priceVolumeSummary: All five major exchanges (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Bitget, Gate) agreed on price: Bitcoin closed around $76,170 and Ethereum around $2,417. Volume was extremely high everywhere, with Binance leading on Bitcoin futures volume and OKX leading on Ethereum.
positioningSummary: Traders were betting on price rises: funding rates stayed positive, meaning those betting on up-moves paid fees (6.6% annualized for Bitcoin, up to 6.7% for Ethereum on some venues). Bitcoin's open interest grew at Binance (+1.2%) but shrank at Bybit (−1.3%), suggesting mixed confidence. Ethereum's open interest rose at most venues. Long positions outnumbered short positions significantly: 1.5 longs per short for Bitcoin and 3.2 for Ethereum on Binance.
stocksSummary: Asian markets fell on September 16. South Korea's stock index dropped 0.94%, led by semiconductor sellers (SK Hynix −0.31%, Samsung −0.34%). Hong Kong was mixed: AI stocks rallied (Zhipu AI +3.3%, MiniMax +9.0%), but Tencent fell 1.5%. China also split: robotics jumped (Unitree +6.6%), while CXMT fell 2.8%. US stocks retreated: S&P 500 −0.44%, Nasdaq flat. Gold surged 1.42% as investors bought safety ahead of the Fed decision, the US dollar strengthened 0.64%, and oil crashed about 3%.

movers.explanation: BR token surged 160% on the day with no clear public news catalyst in available sources.
Harmony's ONE token jumped 56% on the day with no clear public news catalyst in available sources.

topThree.headline: Federal Reserve raises rates by 25 basis points, first hike since July 2023
topThree.what: The Federal Reserve voted unanimously to raise its benchmark interest rate to 3.75%-4.00% on September 16 at 18:00 UTC. This was the central bank's first rate increase since July 2023. Fed officials indicated more hikes are possible but signaled they may slow the pace.

topThree.headline: SEC and CFTC announce plans to regulate crypto without Congress
topThree.what: After the Senate Clarity Act failed, SEC Chair Paul Atkins and CFTC Chair Mike Selig announced their agencies will move forward with crypto regulations using existing authority. The CFTC said it is 'locked in and ready to ship its rules for the new frontier of finance.'

topThree.headline: House committees advance crypto tax bill and Bitcoin reserve bill
topThree.what: Congress voted to advance two bills on September 16: one to reform how cryptocurrency is taxed, exempting qualifying transaction fees from gain calculations; another to create a permanent strategic Bitcoin reserve for the US government. Both advanced along party lines.

Regulation and policy.headline: JPMorgan: Clarity Act not fully dead but passage window extremely narrow
Regulation and policy.what: JPMorgan analysts said the Clarity Act, which failed a Senate vote on September 15, is still technically possible but would require a major political shift to pass before Congress ends.

Regulation and policy.headline: Aave founder pitches DeFi path forward after Clarity Act fails
Regulation and policy.what: Aave founder Stani Kulechov proposed an 'Uber path' for decentralized finance, suggesting the industry could thrive without waiting for regulatory legislation by following how ride-sharing disrupted taxi markets.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Revolut hackers demand $3 million ransom in Monero
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Hackers who breached fintech company Revolut demanded $3 million in Monero (a privacy-focused cryptocurrency) and threatened to sell customer data. The attackers specifically targeted customers with large crypto holdings. Revolut said it has not received direct contact from the attackers.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Hackers hijack HBO Max's Reddit account to spread crypto-stealing malware
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Attackers gained control of HBO Max's verified Reddit account and posted 108 malicious advertisements directing users to fake software downloads designed to steal cryptocurrency wallets.

Traditional markets.headline: Stock market, bonds, and precious metals react to Fed rate hike
Traditional markets.what: On September 16, US stocks fell 0.44% (S&P 500) as the Fed raised rates, while Nasdaq stayed flat. Gold jumped 1.42%, the US dollar strengthened 0.64%, and US Treasury bond prices fell (their yields rose). Oil prices fell about 3%—WTI crude down 3.1%, Brent down 3.05%.

calendarNotes.event: Federal Reserve raises rates by 25 basis points at 18:00–18:30 UTC
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: Rate hikes typically pressure risk assets like cryptocurrency because they make borrowing more expensive and can slow economic growth. On September 16, Bitcoin and Ethereum posted small gains (around 0.7–0.8%), suggesting traders were reassured by Fed comments implying a slower pace of future hikes. The reaction was muted compared to typical rate-hike days.

calendarNotes.event: Retail Sales and Core Retail Sales data at 12:30 UTC
calendarNotes.typicalReaction: Consumer spending figures can move markets, but were overshadowed by the Fed decision later that day.

glossary.definition: One hundredth of a percent (0.01%). Interest rate changes are often described in basis points—for example, a 25 basis point rate hike means a 0.25% increase.

A fee paid between traders on perpetual futures exchanges. When funding is positive, traders betting on price rises pay traders betting on price falls. A higher funding rate means traders are very confident about higher prices.
A bet that an asset's price will go up.
The number of traders betting on price increases divided by the number betting on decreases. A ratio above 1.0 means more traders bet on up than down.
The official reference price an exchange uses for a cryptocurrency at any moment, used to calculate profits and losses on futures contracts.
The total number of active buy and sell contracts (longs and shorts combined) on a futures exchange at any moment.
The percentage increase or decrease in total active contracts on a futures exchange during a time period, showing whether traders are opening new bets or closing old ones.
Cryptocurrency contracts that never expire, allowing traders to bet on price moves using borrowed money (leverage) without a settlement date.
A bet that an asset's price will go down.
